messages.subject: Hierarchical model including diagnostic uncertainty
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to set up a hierarchical model where Y is a latent variable reflecting diagnostic uncertainty (or probability of detection - i.e. a thinned Poisson process). Is this possible to implement this in INLA?

Please let me know if it would help if I provide an example.

Thanks very much

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Hierarchical model including diagnostic uncertainty
parts:
Hi,

it depends on the details of the model, so an example (showing more
precisely what model you would like) might help.

For a thinned Poisson process (as an actual point process) one can do
that in INLA if the log of the thinning probability is linear in some
latent Gaussian variable, or just needs a positive scaling factor,
e.g. a model of the type
eta = log(lambda(x)) + log(p(z;beta))
y ~ Poisson process with intensity exp(eta) (which is the thinned
version of lambda).
log p(z) can be beta * z^2, with beta positive, via the "clinear" model.

For more complicated thinning probability models, where log(p(z))
isn't linear in parameters beta, the inlabru package can be used
instead (inlabru.org).
There one can do models such as log p(z) =
exp(-abs(z/exp(beta1))^exp(beta2)) that aren't linear in beta1 and
beta2.

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Hierarchical model including diagnostic uncertainty
parts:
Hi,

let me write that in (hopefully) more precise mathematical notation,
to make sure I understand what you mean.
Some notation:
- \phi, the density function of a standard N(0,1) variable.
- z, a known (or measured) value for a specific individual
- \pi, u_1, u_2, s_1, s_2, unknown parameters, to be estimated.
- prob(z), the probability (or rather conditional probability) an

prob(z) = \pi \phi[(z-u_1) / s_1] / s_1 / \{ \pi \phi[(z-u_1) / s_1] /
s_1 + (1-\pi) \phi[(z-u_2) / s_2] / s_2 \}

There's a practical difference here if z is a property of the
individual, or if it's a property of a _potential_ individual with
certain characteristics.
Example from ecology:
- the size of a group of dolphins in a property of each specific group
- the roughness of the sea is a property of the ocean in which the dolphins live
Both affect detectability of groups. However, one cannot have group
size without a group, but the state of the
sea at a certain potential group location doesn't care if there is a
group there or not.

In the group size case one needs to model the distribution of group
sizes (possibly with space dependent parameters) explicitly, since one
needs to know what characteristics a specific group that was or
_wasn't_ observed might have.
In the sea state case, one just needs to extend the model into
time-dependent detectability.

I don't quite see how your problem would motivate using the above
probability as a thinning probability for a Poisson process, or what
"z" is, and what the domain of the point process would be. However,
assuming that is what you need, in inlabru you could define a model
with predictor
\eta(s,z) = \log \lambda(s) + \log prob(z)

You would need \pi, u_!, u_2, and s_1, and s_2 to be defined as
transformation of latent gaussian variables, e.g.
\pi = inverselogit(w_1)
u_1 = w_2
u_2 = w_3
s_1 = exp(w_4)
s_2 = exp(w_5)
where each w is a N(0,1) "iid" latent gaussian variable.

The resulting nonlinear model in the w-parameters is linearised iteratively.
In this case, the resulting prob(z) model doesn't look very appealing
to estimate, as it will be hard to identify the parameters, so I'm not
sure how practical this particular approach would be.

Finn
